_comment: TARGET-tier scope definition for a WRAP campaign over libxml2 v2.15.3.
Nothing is targeted: nothing is translated to native Rust. The deliverable
is a safe Rust wrapper over the whole published C API, so the campaign is
defined by the headers that publish it.
_comment_campaign_objective: A WRAP campaign: the `targeted` section composes EMPTY - this campaign owns
nothing - and `imported` is seeded off `api_headers` directly, on
DECLARATION-site membership. `impl_files` is not read at all here; it is
authored anyway, because it describes the library rather than the campaign,
and because flipping this one word to `port` is then the whole edit needed
to turn this into a port campaign.
Seeding off the public headers is what makes wrapping expressible. Entity
classification on a PORT campaign is DEFINITION-anchored, so naming these
headers there would admit only what they DEFINE - inline functions, macros,
value structs - and drop every function they merely DECLARE, whose body sits
in a root .c. As a WRAP seed the test is declaration-site membership
instead, which is the right question for a public header: the bodies live in
files this campaign does not own, and 'does targeted code reach it' has no
answer when nothing is targeted.
Consequences that fall out, with no per-item flag: a struct DEFINED in one
of these headers keeps its full field layout (its fields are the API), one
merely forward-declared stays an opaque handle, symbols order on their
signatures rather than their bodies, and --transitive over an opaque type
pulls nothing it does not need.
`query dag --full` reads this campaign's graph as if it were `port` -
bodies walked, all fields kept - without editing this file.
Ownership analysis is unaffected: ptr_args/ptr_ret come from the T2 tables,
which cover the whole database regardless of scope, so the real bodies are
still what free/store behaviour is read from.
Not the per-wave `translate --objective`, which is the verb one agent is
handed over one selection.
_comment_files: `api_headers` is the seed: 45 headers, 1416 XMLPUBFUN declarations at this
`impl_files` is EMPTY and deliberately so. It is inert under
`campaign_objective: wrap` - nothing reads it - and libxml2 keeps its
sources flat at the repo root (parser.c, tree.c, xmlIO.c, ...) with the
test harness, fuzzers and Python bindings beside them, so there is no
directory entry that names the implementation without also dragging those
in. Filling it is the prerequisite for `query dag --full` here, and it
wants an explicit per-file list, not a `./` walk.
_comment_out_of_scope: `paths` is empty: `api_headers` names only include/libxml/, so the test
harness, fuzzers, Python bindings and examples are outside it by
`features` is documentation only - no composer reads it. It lists the
LIBXML2_WITH_* options OFF in the configure line recorded in build.json.
